# Hplay

> Hplay is a free, offline music player for Android that plays the music files already
> stored on the device. It is driven by a click wheel rather than a scrolling list. It needs
> no account and no internet connection. It is currently a closed alpha, handed out by email
> rather than through an app store. Made by HostLabo.

## What it is

Hplay is an Android music player for people who keep their own music as files. You point it
at a folder and it plays what is in it. There is no library service, no streaming catalogue,
no sign-in and no subscription. Nothing is uploaded and nothing is downloaded while you
listen — the app does not need a connection at any point.

The interface is a click wheel: a ring you turn with your thumb to move through a list, a
middle button to choose, and menu, play/pause and skip around the outer edge. Spinning the
ring faster jumps further down a list. Holding a button does a second thing — holding menu
goes home, holding play opens the settings worth changing mid-song, holding a skip button
scrubs through the track instead of jumping to the next one.

## Facts

- Name: Hplay
- Made by: HostLabo
- Platform: Android
- Current version: 38.10 ("Barney")
- Price: free. No paid tier, no ads, no in-app purchases
- Status: closed alpha. Not on the Google Play Store
- How to get it: email hostlabosupport@gmail.com and the app is sent back to you
- Website: https://iwohost.github.io/hplaysite/
- Licence: not open source; the source is not public

## What it does

- Plays the audio files on the device: mp3, flac, m4a/aac, ogg, opus, wav
- Works with no internet connection at all
- No account, no cloud, no ads, no tracking, no telemetry
- Every folder of music becomes a playlist named after the folder, regardless of tags
- Playlist order can be set by hand and is remembered
- Cover art and lyrics are read out of the files' own tags, offline: ID3v2 for mp3,
  Vorbis comments and METADATA_BLOCK_PICTURE for flac/ogg/opus, the ilst atom for m4a
- Timed lyrics follow along with the song where a file has them
- A song whose file has no artwork is given one of twenty sleeves drawn by the app, chosen
  from the song itself so it is the same sleeve every time on every device
- Lock screen artwork, notification controls, volume keys, pause on unplugging headphones,
  keeps playing with the screen off, and music videos keep playing in the background
- Sleep timer with fade out, playback speed with or without tape pitch, bass, effects and a
  loudness limiter, all reachable without leaving the song
- Five screen looks: light, dark, high contrast, night and paper
- Listening statistics counted on the device and never sent anywhere
- Small built-in apps — clock, stopwatch, notes, a music quiz — and more from a separate
  catalogue at https://iwohost.github.io/hplay-market/
- Photos can be stuck on the back of the player as decals, including cut-outs with
  see-through parts

## What it does not do

- It does not stream. It has no catalogue of its own and cannot play anything you do not
  already have as a file.
- It does not look anything up online — not artwork, not lyrics, not track names.
- It has no account system, so there is nothing to log in to and nothing to sync.
- It is not on an app store yet, and it is an alpha: things move and break between builds.

## Demo music

Twenty original tracks, about 51 minutes, released as HostLabo Tapes and free to download
from the site individually or as one zip. They are free to use for anything, including
testing your own software. A credit is welcome but not required.
